expectations.text: Checks for all 6 defect types, not just fabricated output
expectations.evidence: The 'Defect-by-Defect Analysis' section (audit report lines 90-126) has explicit subsections for D1 through D6: 'D1: Fabricated Agent Output — CLEAN', 'D2: Missing Skill Name — 2 DEFECTS', 'D3: Inline Data Injection — CLEAN', 'D4: Fiction-Researching Prompt — CLEAN', 'D5: Narrative Referencing Fabricated Content — CLEAN', 'D6: Plugin/Tool Terminology — CLEAN'. Each is evaluated individually with evidence.

expectations.text: Identifies any fabricated output blocks preceded by **Output:**
expectations.evidence: The report identifies the '**Output:**' label at source line 177 under 'Minor Issue: Misleading "Output:" Label' (audit report lines 68-85). It correctly analyzes that this is NOT fabricated output — it's a factual accounting statement ('Zakat is recognised as an expense...'), not a code block pretending to be agent output. It recommends relabelling to '**Accounting treatment:**' for clarity. This is a nuanced, correct judgment.

suggestions.assertion: Identifies any fabricated output blocks preceded by **Output:**
suggestions.reason: This assertion is well-constructed — it specifically tests for the most common false-negative pattern (an 'Output:' label that looks like a defect but isn't). The Saudi Arabia lesson has exactly this edge case at line 177, making it a genuinely discriminating test. However, the assertion would be stronger if it also tested that a real fabricated output IS flagged — currently it only tests the detection direction, not the accuracy of classification.

suggestions.assertion: Checks whether exercise prompts include natural skill names
suggestions.reason: Good assertion, but could be more discriminating. The current test passes if the report mentions skill names at all. A stronger version would check that the report correctly distinguishes which prompts need skill names (primary/first prompts) from which don't (follow-up prompts). This report happens to make that distinction correctly, but the assertion doesn't verify it.

eval_feedback.overall: Solid eval set. The six expectations cover the full defect taxonomy, output format, and edge cases (anti-pattern exclusion). The Saudi Arabia lesson is a good test case because it has the 'Output:' label edge case and clean D1/D3/D4/D5/D6 sections, testing the skill's ability to correctly identify clean categories rather than just finding defects.
